name: Arseniy Vershinin
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect (formerly CTO), Personio
profile: Russian-born software engineer who co-founded Munich HR-software company Personio in 2015 with Hanno Renner, Roman Schumacher and Ignaz Forstmeier, serving as CTO as it grew into Europe's leading SMB HR platform (valued up to $8.5B). In a 2024 leadership change he moved from CTO to Chief Architect, leading technology projects.
interesting_fact: He met his three Personio co-founders in 2014 at Munich's Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM), a one-year startup program for TUM/LMU students.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Ulan-Ude and raised in the small Siberian town of Ust-Ilimsk, he spent a year in the US as a teen on the FLEX exchange program, then studied at MIPT ('Phystech') and did iOS development for Moscow startups before moving to Munich for 'an international atmosphere'.
notes: Low public profile; listed as a Founders Pledge member (https://www.founderspledge.com/members/2681). Best route is Personio press office. Could not directly re-verify the press email in the PDF (download blocked); also seen as press@personio.de on older releases.

name: Tanel Suurhans
current_role: Co-founder and Distinguished Engineer, ID.me (CTO 2014-2024)
profile: Estonian engineer who joined veterans' discount startup TroopSwap as co-founder in 2013 and helped rebuild it as ID.me, the digital identity wallet used by US federal and state agencies (valued ~$2B in 2021). He was CTO from 2014 until September 2024, when Scott Meyer succeeded him and he moved to Distinguished Engineer.
interesting_fact: Tallinn's city government celebrated ID.me as 'yet another unicorn co-founded by an Estonian', citing it as proof of Estonia's world-leading unicorn-per-capita record.
deep_cut_fact: ID.me began in 2010 as TroopSwap, a service founded by two former Army Rangers to verify veterans for discounts; Suurhans was brought on in 2013 as the Estonian technical co-founder who helped turn that log-in flow into a general identity network.
notes: Very low public profile; no published personal or press email found for ID.me (media seems routed through staff contacts). CTO transition source: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/idme-appoints-scott-meyer-as-chief-technology-officer-302242142.html

name: Rotem Iram
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, At-Bay (acquired by Munich Re, Aug 2026)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded cyber-insurance company At-Bay in 2016 with former McKinsey colleague Roman Itskovich; it pioneered 'InsurSec', pairing insurance with security scanning and monitoring, and hit a $1.35B valuation in 2021. Munich Re bought At-Bay for $575M in August 2026; Iram is based in Tel Aviv again after a decade in Palo Alto.
interesting_fact: He first ran into the cyber-insurance problem while at risk consultancy K2 Integrity after the Target data breach, which led to At-Bay's model of underwriting using external scans of client systems.
deep_cut_fact: Before McKinsey he was an officer in IDF Unit 8200 and a software engineer at RAD Data Communications, holds a computer-engineering BSc from the Hebrew University, and grew up in Herzliya after a childhood stint at Kibbutz Lehavot HaBashan.
notes: Recent exit to Munich Re (Calcalist, Oct 2026) was below peak valuation - avoid framing around valuation. WEF contributor (https://weforum.org/stories/authors/rotem-iram).

name: Nishant Mungali
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Mindtickle
profile: Indian product designer-turned-founder who co-founded Mindtickle (Pune/San Francisco) in 2011 with Krishna Depura, Mohit Garg and Deepak Diwakar. The company grew from gamified onboarding into a sales-readiness and revenue-enablement platform, reaching unicorn status in 2021 (~$1.2B); he leads product.
interesting_fact: He recalls that at launch Mindtickle 'had difficulty landing one client, let alone five' and leaned on its network and a pilot program for its first referenceable customers.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Almora in the Kumaon hills of Uttarakhand, he studied at IIT Guwahati and took his first job at investment firm D. E. Shaw in Hyderabad (as a UX designer) before the four co-founders started dabbling with the Mindtickle idea in 2010.
notes: Mindtickle 2025 releases name individual media contacts without emails; older releases show a generic pr(at)mindtickle address that I could not confirm on a live page, so not listed. Route via Mindtickle newsroom (https://www.mindtickle.com/blog/news_tax/news).

name: Arad Levertov
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Sunbit
profile: Israeli-born fintech founder who co-founded Sunbit in 2016 (with Tal Riesenfeld, Ornit Dweck-Maizel and Prof. Tamir Hazan) after serving as COO/EVP at online lender Enova and earlier at Intel. Sunbit offers point-of-sale 'pay-over-time' financing at dentists, auto-service shops and other everyday merchants; it was valued at $1.1B in 2021 and completed its first $200M ABS deal in 2025.
interesting_fact: Named an EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2025 Greater Los Angeles award winner.
deep_cut_fact: He has said a personal experience of being rejected for a credit card - which he found humiliating - was a major reason he started Sunbit, whose pitch is approving people with thin credit files.
notes: Has done many podcasts (Mixergy, DealMakers, Fintech Business Weekly) - receptive to founder-story interviews. Reported military background varies between sources; not used.

name: Nuno Sebastiao
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Feedzai
profile: Portuguese engineer who co-founded AI fraud-prevention company Feedzai (Coimbra/San Mateo) in 2011, growing it into Portugal's fourth unicorn, used by major banks and payment firms. In October 2025 Feedzai was selected by the ECB to provide fraud detection for the forthcoming digital euro and raised $75M at a $2B valuation.
interesting_fact: Feedzai was chosen by the European Central Bank as the fraud-detection and prevention provider for the future digital euro (Oct 2025).
deep_cut_fact: Before Feedzai he spent 2006-2010 as a product manager at the European Space Agency in Germany, leading development of its Satellite Simulation Infrastructure; earlier he founded a startup doing software validation for aerospace. He holds MBAs from both London Business School and UCLA, and a CS degree from Coimbra.
notes: Active speaker/podcast guest on fraud and AI. PR email appears in syndicated Oct 2025 release (page blocked to direct fetch; per search snippet).

name: Saurabh Garg
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Business Officer, NoBroker.com
profile: IIT and IIM Ahmedabad (PGP 2004) alumnus who co-founded Bengaluru-based NoBroker in 2014 with Amit Kumar Agarwal and Akhil Gupta to let Indians rent and buy property without paying broker commissions. NoBroker became India's first proptech unicorn (~$1B, 2021) and has expanded into home services and society-management (NoBrokerHood); Garg is also an angel investor in 30+ startups.
interesting_fact: He has said he first felt the problem in 2007, when he struggled to find accommodation in Mumbai without paying a large broker fee.
deep_cut_fact: He attempted startups while at IIT during the dot-com boom, then turned down master's-in-finance offers from LSE and Columbia to attend IIM Ahmedabad to learn 'how companies are built'; IIMA later gave him its Young Alumni Achievers' Award (YAAA 2022).
notes: Regular speaker at IITs/IIMs/incubators - open to talks. No verified press email found (only a redacted address on YourStory). Sources differ on whether his IIT was Bombay or Delhi; omitted.

name: Vamsi Krishna
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Vedantu
profile: IIT graduate who, with Pulkit Jain and Anand Prakash, founded IIT-JEE coaching venture Lakshya in 2006 (acquired by MT Educare in 2012) and then co-founded live online tutoring platform Vedantu in 2014. Vedantu became a unicorn in 2021 (~$1B) and he continues to lead it as CEO through the post-pandemic edtech reset, including offline/hybrid expansion.
interesting_fact: Vedantu was explicitly designed to be 'a 10x better version of Lakshya at a quarter of the cost', with the aim of 'glamourising the teaching profession'.
deep_cut_fact: His teaching career began around 2006 when he and his co-founders mentored a batch of about 35 children from factory-worker families; 11 of them got into the IITs, the turning point that led to Lakshya and later Vedantu.
notes: Common name - make sure outreach references Vedantu. No published press email found. Edtech sector downturn since 2022; avoid valuation framing.

name: David Fenkel
current_role: Co-founder, A24
profile: Independent-film executive who co-founded A24 in 2012 with Daniel Katz and John Hodges after running Oscilloscope Laboratories with the Beastie Boys' Adam Yauch. A24 became the defining indie studio (Moonlight, Everything Everywhere All at Once), raised capital at a ~$3.5B valuation in 2024, and he remains a co-leader alongside Katz.
interesting_fact: A24 won Best Picture twice in six years - Moonlight (2017) and Everything Everywhere All at Once, which swept seven Oscars in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He met Adam Yauch as a THINKFilm executive when the company financed and released the Beastie Boys' fan-shot concert film 'Awesome; I F*ckin' Shot That!' (2006); Yauch then recruited him to run his new film distributor Oscilloscope, whose first release was the documentary 'Gunnin' for That #1 Spot'.
notes: Famously press-shy; A24 executives rarely give interviews. No published press email for him; A24 publicity is handled per film.

name: Lindsay Kaplan
current_role: Co-founder, Chief; venture partner at Bullish (2026)
profile: American entrepreneur and brand marketer who co-founded Chief, the private membership network for senior executive women, with Carolyn Childers. Chief raised $100M in 2022 at a $1B+ valuation, one of the fastest women-founded companies to unicorn status. She is also an angel investor, an investing partner at Next Wave NYC (2024) and, from 2026, a venture partner at Bullish.

profile: Co-founder and CTO of Austin-based ICON, which builds large-scale robotic 3D printers (Vulcan), materials and software for printing homes and structures, including work for NASA on lunar and Mars construction.
